name: Datadog
summary: External observability service capability for approved logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, monitors, and runtime instrumentation evidence.

source.notes: Registered as a governed observability capability. This entry does not create a Datadog account, add SDK code, transmit telemetry, or approve paid usage by itself.

useWhen: A ticket requires observability planning for code, infrastructure, automation, runtime cockpit, agent runs, delivery evidence, or customer-facing product behavior.
A PRD, architecture review, risk review, tactical execution plan, or delivery handoff needs logging, metrics, traces, dashboards, monitor, alert, or error-reporting requirements.
A production or beta workflow needs approved operational telemetry with explicit data minimization, retention, and cost boundaries.
doNotUseWhen: The ticket does not include observability, instrumentation, runtime monitoring, or delivery evidence scope.
Telemetry would include secrets, credentials, raw customer data, raw interview data, private evidence, production data, or sensitive personal data without explicit approval and retention rules.
Datadog output would be treated as customer validation, market demand, product-market fit, or canonical knowledge base.
Paid usage, new account setup, SDK installation, or external data transmission is implied but not approved.
routing.fallback: Define repository-native observability requirements, sample event shapes, and manual validation evidence. Record a Datadog follow-up if credentials, paid use, or telemetry transmission is not approved.

inputs.name: observabilityNeed
inputs.description: The operational question the telemetry must answer, such as error rate, latency, run state, cost/session, customer-facing funnel behavior, or delivery evidence.
inputs.sourceOrDestination: PRD, architecture review, tactical execution plan, delivery evidence, or Linear ticket

inputs.name: dataBoundary
inputs.description: Approved statement of what data may and may not be sent to Datadog, including PII, customer data, production data, secrets, and retention constraints.
inputs.sourceOrDestination: Risk review, security/privacy gate, architecture review, or human approval

inputs.name: runtimeSurface
inputs.description: Service, workflow, agent run, product environment, or manual test surface to observe.

outputs.name: observabilityPlan
outputs.description: Approved telemetry plan covering signals, event shape, dashboard or monitor needs, owner, threshold, and validation method.
outputs.sourceOrDestination: Architecture review, tactical execution plan, or delivery handoff

outputs.name: datadogReference
outputs.description: Dashboard, monitor, log query, trace view, or Datadog configuration reference when actual Datadog use is approved and performed.
outputs.sourceOrDestination: Linear handoff, PR, or delivery evidence

schemas.notes: Future observability adapter work may define a normalized ObservabilitySignal or DatadogReference schema if multiple agents need machine-readable telemetry evidence.

allowedOperations: Propose log, metric, trace, dashboard, monitor, and alert shapes
Reference approved Datadog dashboards, monitors, log queries, or traces
Use approved Datadog telemetry as delivery, runtime, or operational evidence
forbiddenOperations: Create or configure Datadog accounts without approval
Transmit telemetry, logs, traces, metrics, or events without approved credentials and data boundary
Send secrets, credentials, private customer data, raw interview data, raw recordings, or sensitive production data
Treat Datadog telemetry as market validation, customer demand proof, or canonical knowledge base
Start or expand paid usage without approval

cost.costDriver: Datadog plan, ingested logs/metrics/traces, retention, dashboards, monitors, hosts, sessions, and product-specific instrumentation volume.

risks.description: Telemetry can accidentally include customer data, production data, secrets, private evidence, or sensitive workflow details.
risks.mitigation: Require data minimization, redaction, retention boundaries, and explicit approval before transmitting data.

risks.description: Ingestion and retention volume can create unexpected usage-based cost.
risks.mitigation: Require paid-use approval, event sampling or volume limits, retention review, and cost/session monitoring before broad instrumentation.

risks.description: Operational telemetry can be misread as product-market fit, customer demand, or market validation.
risks.mitigation: Use Datadog for runtime and delivery evidence only. Market validation still requires approved discovery and validation artifacts.

risks.description: Datadog pricing, product capabilities, APIs, and permissions can change.
risks.mitigation: Review the registry entry before production rollout, paid use, or adapter implementation.

approvalTriggers: Creating or changing Datadog account, project, dashboard, monitor, alert, API key, or SDK integration
Sending telemetry, logs, traces, metrics, events, errors, sessions, or production data to Datadog
Using paid Datadog features or increasing ingestion volume
Capturing customer, production, private, security, compliance, or sensitive data
Using Datadog evidence to support launch, scale, reliability, or customer-facing claims
governance.dataBoundary: Datadog may receive only approved, minimized operational telemetry. It must not receive secrets, credentials, raw customer interviews, raw recordings, raw transcripts, private founder notes, or sensitive customer/production data unless a dedicated ticket records approval, retention, and redaction rules.
governance.sensitiveActionBoundary: Datadog is observability, not knowledge base, validation proof, approval authority, or customer evidence source. It cannot override Market Validation Before Code, PR review, Linear governance, or human approval gates.
governance.loggingRequirement: Record signal names, data fields, environment, dashboard or monitor references, owner, threshold, approval status, cost boundary, and residual privacy risk in the PR or Linear handoff.
governance.updatePolicy: Review before first production use, before paid use, before customer-data telemetry, and whenever Datadog product behavior, credentials, pricing, or retention settings change.

review.reviewNotes: Pilot observability capability. Planning and references are allowed under ticket scope; real Datadog mutation, SDK integration, data transmission, or paid use requires explicit approval.

examples.scenario: A build ticket adds a background agent workflow and needs delivery evidence for run failures and retries.
examples.expectedUse: Define Datadog log, metric, dashboard, or monitor requirements and use approved telemetry references in the delivery handoff after data boundaries are approved.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not send raw prompts, secrets, customer data, or private evidence to Datadog while implementing the workflow.

examples.scenario: A founder asks whether early interview feedback proves the market wants the product.
examples.expectedUse: Do not route to Datadog; use validation and interview evidence artifacts instead.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not treat product telemetry, dashboards, or event counts as market validation without the required discovery evidence.
